# Anvil — interactive labs (https://edu.hartwell-labs.pl)

> Hartwell Labs' interactive platform: cybersecurity, Python, Ruby and Rust. Write code,
> > it runs in your browser (Python through WebAssembly), and the checker tells you which
> > test failed. Labs that need a real machine run in a downloadable lab VM.
Generated 2026-10-16. Machine-readable task manifest: https://edu.hartwell-labs.pl/api/manifest

## Access model

- **An account is required** to open any lab (`POST /api/auth/register`: nickname,
  e-mail, client-side password verifier). One confirmation e-mail is sent;
  `GET /api/auth/verify?token=…` confirms the address.
- **The first ten labs are free** with that account and stay free.
- **The second tier (`plan = "lifetime"`) opens the remaining six labs** — the full
  paths: sliding-window rate limiting, a scanner built to a spec, a safe eBPF FFI
  wrapper, borrow-checker depth, and the service you have to run yourself. No price
  list: quoted per conversation, lifetime (one payment, not a subscription).
- Sessions: 32 random bytes in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie, 60-day expiry.
- Passwords are stretched in the browser (PBKDF2-SHA256, 210 000 iterations); only the
  verifier reaches the server, which compares it in constant time.
- `GET /api/manifest` returns all 16 tasks with a `free` flag. `GET /api/me` returns
  profile, plan, progress and streak.

## Pages

- [Home](https://edu.hartwell-labs.pl/): tracks, how it works, the lab VM
- [Lab](https://edu.hartwell-labs.pl/lab): the runner — sign in, pick a track, write code, run it
- [Lab VM](https://edu.hartwell-labs.pl/lab-vm/README.md): the downloadable machine for systems labs
- [Build script](https://edu.hartwell-labs.pl/lab-vm/build.sh): builds the image or runs it in host mode
- [Task manifest](https://edu.hartwell-labs.pl/api/manifest): every task as JSON

## Execution model

| Executor | Meaning | Where it runs |
|---|---|---|
| `pyodide` | Python 3 in WebAssembly | learner's browser, runtime served from this domain |
| `quiz` | one correct answer, no code | browser |
| `vm` | needs a kernel, network or compiler | downloaded lab VM, verified locally by `labcheck` |

## Free labs (first ten)

### Python

- **Turn a log line into structure** (`py-01-authlog`, difficulty 1, 100 pts, pyodide) — A log line looks like `IP - - [ts] "METHOD path" status`. Complete `parse_line` so it returns a tuple `(ip, method, status)` with `status` as an `int`. Empty line... 7 assertions, 3 hints, one Stretch goal.
- **Verify a checksum** (`py-02-digest`, difficulty 2, 120 pts, pyodide) — You have the file bytes and an expected digest. Complete `sha256_hex` so it returns the hex digest. **Watch the trap**: unbounded `int(digest, 16)` comparisons br... 6 assertions, 3 hints, one Stretch goal.
- **Three layers of encryption** (`py-03-decoder`, difficulty 2, 150 pts, pyodide) — The payload is base64, under it ROT13, under that a reversed string. Complete `decode_blob` so it returns the plaintext. Two gotchas: `base64.b64decode` needs byt... 5 assertions, 3 hints, one Stretch goal.
- **Decode a JWT and spot the unsigned one** (`py-05-jwt`, difficulty 3, 190 pts, pyodide) — A JWT is three base64**url** parts separated by dots. Complete `decode_payload` so it returns the payload as a dictionary, and `is_unsigned` so it reports a token... 8 assertions, 3 hints, one Stretch goal.

### Cybersecurity

- **Spot an injection attempt** (`py-04-sqli`, difficulty 3, 180 pts, pyodide) — You get part of an HTTP query. Complete `is_injection` so it returns `True` when the value looks like a SQL injection attempt: `' OR`, `" OR`, `UNION SELECT`, `;... 8 assertions, 3 hints, one Stretch goal.
- **Redact a card number in a log** (`rb-02-redact`, difficulty 2, 140 pts, vm) — Masking card numbers is real work in logs and incident reports, so this lab starts in the downloadable lab machine. Verified by `labcheck` on the lab VM.
- **Name the technique in the log** (`sec-01-technique`, difficulty 2, 120 pts, quiz) — A fragment of a WAF log from your own environment: Verified by `labcheck` on the lab VM.
- **Count who is hammering the service** (`py-06-ipgrep`, difficulty 2, 150 pts, pyodide) — A firewall log, one line per request. Complete `top_ips` so it returns the addresses seen **at least `threshold` times** (the default is 2 — anything seen once is... 6 assertions, 3 hints, one Stretch goal.

### Ruby

- **Enumerable where a loop would go** (`rb-01-enumerable`, difficulty 2, 130 pts, vm) — This track needs a real interpreter, so in v1 the Ruby labs run in the downloadable lab machine. Verified by `labcheck` on the lab VM.

### Rust

- **Predict the output: ownership** (`rs-01-predict`, difficulty 3, 160 pts, quiz) — Rust does not compile in the browser, but the compiler is still the best teacher of ownership. Which of these programs **compiles**? Verified by `labcheck` on the lab VM.

## Paid tier — lifetime

- **Sliding-window rate limiting** (`py-07-ratelimit`, difficulty 4, 240 pts, pyodide) — fixed buckets are the classic bug: a burst split across a boundary gets twice the budget.
- **Read a borrow checker error** (`rs-02-panic`, difficulty 4, 180 pts, quiz) — `v.push(v.len())`, pick the clean fix, 6 options.
- **Predict the output: a reference outlives its owner** (`rs-03-borrow`, difficulty 4, 190 pts, quiz) — E0515, returning `&local`, 6 options.
- **Run a service with an unsafe flag** (`vm-01-insecure-flag`, difficulty 3, 200 pts, vm) — set a flag that leaks a secret into the log and confirm it with one command.
- **Write your own scanner with ShadowScan** (`sec-l1-webscan`, difficulty 5, 600 pts, vm) — scope, request budget, sorted and diffable output; `labcheck` rejects out-of-scope results.
- **Safe FFI to eBPF** (`rs-l1-ffi`, difficulty 5, 900 pts, vm) — wrap `bpf_probe_read_user` so a caller never gets a half-filled buffer; `labcheck` builds and runs your tests.
